If they won't let our lorries out, theirs can wait with ours. Bring a sandwich.

choices.label: Send the consul with food and blankets, and keep talking

lines.text: Food and blankets today, a deal tomorrow. Nobody pays a bribe on our behalf.
First get them a hot meal and a shower. Then argue.
One day that border will be a ten-minute stop. We get there by talking, even now.

choices.label: Blame the government for letting them push us around

lines.text: Eleven days! A country that can't get its own drivers home doesn't deserve a foreign ministry!
The minister found time for a holiday this month. Not for forty drivers.
The Trueants test us because they know this government won't answer.

EVENTS.title: Four {national} aid workers taken hostage in Norbanistan
EVENTS.text: A militia in northern Norbanistan has seized four volunteers from a Cranebo medical charity. It wants two million Golban dollars. The families are camped outside the foreign ministry.

choices.label: Say {country} never pays ransom

lines.text: Pay once, and every {national} abroad becomes a price tag. We bring them home another way.
Not one pezo for gunmen! Find them and bring them back!
If you pay the wolf, he comes back for the rest of the flock.

choices.label: Bring them home, whatever it costs

lines.text: They went to save lives. The least their country can do is save theirs.
If it were my daughter, I'd sell the house. They're somebody's daughters.
Four people who went to help strangers. I want to live in the country that brings them home.

choices.label: Say they knew the risks when they went

lines.text: Our sympathy is with the families, but the state cannot underwrite every private journey into a war zone.
There's plenty of people to help in Fauran, and nobody gets kidnapped.

choices.label: Work quietly with the government, and say nothing

EVENTS.title: A Golban data centre wants {province}'s water
EVENTS.text: A Golban tech firm plans a huge data centre for its AI models in {province}. It would use as much water as a town of eighty thousand people, during a dry decade. It promises three hundred jobs and a new school.

choices.label: Welcome it: {country} can't miss the future

lines.text: Every country is competing for these centres. Turn this one away, and it goes to Dillihan.
Three hundred jobs and a new school. In {province}, that's a lot.
Let {country} be where the future gets built, not where it gets downloaded.

choices.label: Allow it only if it recycles its water and pays local prices

lines.text: Build it, but on our terms: recycled water, full price, and the jobs go to local people.
They can have the land. The water, they pay for like the rest of us.
A centre that cools itself and teaches our kids to code. That's a deal worth signing.

choices.label: Say farms need the water more than computers

lines.text: In a dry decade, water goes to the people who grow our food. That's not anti-technology, it's arithmetic.
They want our water so a Golban computer can write poems!
You can't eat an algorithm. I checked.

EVENTS.title: Banks replace six thousand call-centre jobs with AI
EVENTS.text: The country's three biggest banks will close their call centres in Tarroport by next year and answer customers with AI. Six thousand jobs go, most held by women over forty. Customers say the machine is already more polite.

choices.label: Tax companies that replace workers with AI

lines.text: If a machine takes a job, it can pay some of the tax the worker paid.
Six thousand jobs gone so three banks can save on coffee breaks!
I rang my bank last week. The robot was very nice. It still couldn't find my money.

choices.label: Promise to retrain every one of them

lines.text: Every worker who loses a job to a machine gets a year's training on full pay.
Nobody in Tarroport is too old to learn. My aunt learned to text at seventy.
These six thousand could be running the machines in five years. Let's pay for that.

choices.label: Say it's progress and {country} must keep up

lines.text: The countries that adopt this first will be the rich ones in twenty years.
Machines that answer phones free people to do the work machines can't.
We didn't save the switchboard operators either.

EVENTS.title: Missing girl found dead near {city}
EVENTS.text: Mila, eight, went missing on her way home from school in {city} nine days ago. Her body was found this morning in a field outside town. Police have arrested a 41-year-old farmhand. He was born in Norbanistan. The whole country is in mourning.

choices.label: Visit the family privately, and say nothing in public
Ask why the search took nine days

lines.text: Her family deserves to know why it took nine days. So does every parent in {country}.
Nine days! The police found a minister's stolen car in nine hours last year!
I don't want a speech from the police chief. I want to know what happened on day one.

choices.label: Say this is what open borders cost

lines.text: How many more children before this government finds out who it let in?
We must ask, calmly, how a man with his past came to be living next to a primary school.
Mila would be alive if our borders were closed. Every one of you knows it.

choices.label: Call for calm until the trial

lines.text: A man has been arrested. Let the courts judge him, not the crowd.
Tonight hold your children, and leave the rest to the court.

EVENTS.title: Influencers turn on you
EVENTS.text: Barbara Lulli and Jeremy Hannigan, who never talk politics, posted a joint video: "We don't do this, but the things that party says about people are hateful, and our followers should know." Six million views by lunchtime.

choices.label: Admit you went too far, and soften

lines.text: Some of what I said was wrong, and the way I said it was worse. I'll do better.
My mother saw the video. Believe me, they're not the hardest critics I've faced today.
I want a country where everyone feels at home, and I haven't always sounded like it. That changes now.

choices.label: Say rich influencers don't know real life

lines.text: A gamer and a café blogger lecture working families about hate? Spare us!
I respect their right to their views. I don't need their permission to speak for people they never meet.
Come to Bayernal on a Tuesday, Jeremy. Bring your headphones, it gets loud.

choices.label: Ignore it

EVENTS.title: A mural of you appears in {city}
EVENTS.text: Overnight, artists painted a mural four storeys high on a wall in {city}: you, in a suit, feeding a bonfire with books in every language spoken in {country}. Thousands came to photograph it. Three more appeared by the weekend.

choices.label: Go and see it, and laugh it off

lines.text: They got my good side. I didn't know I had one.
Art that makes people argue is doing its job. I've come to look, not to complain.
If they paint me differently in a year, I'll come back and take a photo with that one too.

choices.label: Demand the city paint over it

lines.text: That wall is somebody's property. Defacing it is a crime, whatever it shows.
Vandals with paint cans don't get to slander a party of the people!
If I painted my opinion on your house, you'd call the police too.

choices.label: Say it proves the cultural elite fears you

lines.text: They paint walls. We knock on doors. Let's see who gets the votes.
Four storeys, all for me. My mother says it's the nicest thing they've ever done.
When the arts world spends this much paint on one party, it tells you who they're afraid of.

EVENTS.title: A Dillihan drama is the most-watched show in {country}
EVENTS.text: "The Orchard Wars", a Dillihan family drama about feuding fruit farmers, is the most-watched show in the country. Babies are being named after its characters. Fauran farmers point out that the orchards in it look exactly like theirs.

choices.label: Say you're watching it too

lines.text: I'm on season two. Don't tell me what happens to the uncle.
Good stories cross borders. One day the whole region will be watching ours.
It's a fine series. Our neighbours can make good television; so can we.

choices.label: Fund {national} drama to compete

lines.text: If Dillihan can make the country's favourite show, so can we, with the right support.
We have feuding farmers too. Ours have better jokes.
The next show the whole region watches should be filmed in Fauran. Let's pay for that.

choices.label: Call for quotas on foreign television

lines.text: Half of what's on our screens should be made here. Plenty of countries do it.
Dillihan wants our pastures and our living rooms!
Dillihan patrols take our cattle in the day, and their dramas take our evenings.

EVENTS.title: Rats in the kitchen that feeds two hundred schools
EVENTS.text: Inspectors found rat droppings and spoiled meat at the central kitchen that supplies lunches to two hundred schools in Cranbia. It was last inspected four years ago. The number of food inspectors has halved since 2022.

choices.label: Promise to hire back the inspectors

lines.text: Every kitchen that feeds children gets inspected every year. That means hiring the inspectors back.
They cut the inspectors to save money and fed the savings to our children!
My kids eat there. I want an inspector in that kitchen more often than the rats.
School lunch should be the best meal some kids eat all day. Let's make it that.

choices.label: Ban the company and sue its owners

lines.text: The company loses every public contract it holds, and its owners answer in court.
Lock the doors and put the owners in front of a judge!
If my restaurant served that, I'd be closed by teatime. Same rules for them.

choices.label: Say parents should pack their children's lunches

lines.text: Families know best what their children should eat. The state needn't run a kitchen for every school.
My mother packed my lunch for twelve years. Nobody ever found a rat in it.

EVENTS.title: Cranebo inspectors ban Fauran's raw-milk cheese
EVENTS.text: New hygiene rules from Cranebo ban the sale of cheese made from raw milk. In Fauran, villages have made it the same way for four hundred years. The cheesemakers have been told to buy stainless steel tanks they can't afford.

choices.label: Defend the cheesemakers: exempt traditional food

lines.text: Traditional food made the traditional way deserves its own rules, written with the people who make it.
Four hundred years of cheese, and a clerk in Cranebo knows better!
My grandfather ate that cheese every day and lived to ninety-one. He'd have lived to a hundred if they'd let him.
Let's make Fauran cheese famous across the region instead of illegal at home.

choices.label: Back the rules: safety comes first

lines.text: Raw milk can make children seriously ill. Rules for food safety can't depend on where you live.
I like old cheese. I don't like old bacteria.

choices.label: Offer grants to help them meet the rules

lines.text: Keep the rules, and pay for the tanks. Safety shouldn't cost a village its living.
If Cranebo wants shiny tanks in Fauran, Cranebo can help buy them.
Same cheese, same villages, cleaner tanks. Fauran can have both.

EVENTS.title: The river below {city} runs orange
EVENTS.text: For three days the river below {city} has run orange. Dead fish line the banks for twenty kilometres. A chemical plant upstream admits a "discharge incident". It employs 1,800 people in a town of forty thousand.

choices.label: Close the plant until it's cleaned up

lines.text: The plant reopens when it can prove it won't happen again. Not a day before.
They poisoned a river and called it an incident. Shut it down!
My kids used to swim there. Now the fish are floating on their backs.
In five years that river can be clean enough to swim in again. It starts with closing the pipe.

choices.label: Fine them heavily, but keep the jobs

lines.text: A fine big enough to hurt, a clean-up they pay for, and eighteen hundred jobs kept.
Make them pay for every fish. And keep the town working.

choices.label: Make the owners personally pay

lines.text: The owners live upstream of nothing. Let them pay out of their own pockets!
When a company poisons a river, the people who run it should answer personally, in court.
I'd like to see the chairman's garden pond turn orange. Just for a week.

EVENTS.title: Calls to ban "Black Harbour" after school knife fights
EVENTS.text: Two pupils were stabbed in school fights in Tarroport this month. Teachers say boys copy the gang drama "Black Harbour", the country's most-watched series among teenagers. A group of parents wants it banned.

choices.label: Ban it from television and the apps

lines.text: Children are copying what they see. Some things don't belong on a screen in every bedroom.
They sell knives to our kids as entertainment! Take it off the air!
When my son started talking like a gangster at breakfast, I knew it had gone too far.

choices.label: Defend it: banning a show solves nothing

lines.text: Knife fights existed before television. Banning a series lets us avoid asking why.
They banned a comic when I was a boy. We read it under the bed.
Our kids are smarter than we give them credit for. Talk to them, don't switch them off.

choices.label: Say boys need somewhere to go, not a ban

lines.text: A boy with a football club on a Tuesday night isn't watching gang dramas for ideas.
Bored fifteen-year-olds will copy anything. Give them something better to copy.
Every kid in Tarroport with a coach, a team and somewhere to be. That's what beats Black Harbour.

EVENTS.title: Three women killed by former partners in one week
EVENTS.text: Three women were killed by former partners this week, in Cranebo, Nikecisa and Kansilia. All three had gone to the police. Two had restraining orders. Thousands marched in silence last night; the question now is who failed them.

choices.label: Blame the police: they were warned and did nothing

lines.text: Three women asked the police for help. Every one of those reports must be investigated, and someone must answer.
They went to the police and were sent home! How many warnings does it take?
My sister reported a man once. The officer asked what she'd done to upset him.
A woman who goes to the police should walk out safer than she walked in. We can build that.

choices.label: Blame soft courts: tougher sentences

lines.text: A restraining order means nothing if breaking it costs nothing. Breaking one should mean prison.
Two of them had court orders! The courts gave those men a piece of paper and a second chance!
A restraining order is a sheet of paper. Paper never stopped anybody.

choices.label: Blame a culture that treats women as property

lines.text: This doesn't start with a knife. It starts with jokes, with silence, with 'it's a family matter'.
Men who think they own women are made, not born. Ask who made them!
Our daughters can grow up in a country where this is unthinkable. It's up to us, all of us.
Listen to the four-hour podcasts our sons are listening to, and you'll understand this week.

choices.label: Blame men from abroad

lines.text: Ask where these men came from, and who let them in!
We must ask whether some of the men coming to {country} share our values about women.

EVENTS.title: Interior minister asked who looks after her children
EVENTS.text: On live television, the interviewer asked Interior Minister Claire Anderson, in the middle of a border crisis, who looks after her two children while she works such long hours. Nobody has ever asked her male colleagues. The clip is everywhere.

choices.label: Call the question out

lines.text: Ask her about the border. That's her job, and it's the question the country needs answered.
In twenty years nobody has asked a male minister who minds his kids. Not once!
I've been asked about my party, my money and my tie. Never about who's feeding my children.
One day that question will sound as strange as asking her if she can read. Let's get there quickly.

choices.label: Say it's a fair question for any parent

lines.text: Every parent in public life should be asked how they balance it. Fathers too.
My mother would have asked her the same thing. Then she'd have offered to babysit.

choices.label: Stay out of it: you'd rather talk about the border

lines.text: I'll leave the interviewers to argue among themselves. The border is the story.

EVENTS.title: Mario Goranov: women are "too emotional for a crisis"
EVENTS.text: On his four-hour podcast, Mario Goranov told a million listeners, most of them young men, that women in government are "too emotional to lead in a crisis". He has invited every party leader on his show next week. Two have already said yes.

choices.label: Condemn it, and refuse his invitation

lines.text: Half the people who kept this country running through every crisis were women. I won't sit next to someone who says otherwise.
My grandmother ran a farm through a drought and a war. Mr Goranov can tell her about emotions.
Our daughters should grow up thinking that's a strange thing to say. I'd like to help with that.

choices.label: Go on the show anyway: his listeners vote too

lines.text: I'll go where the voters are. I won't agree with everything said in the studio.
A million young men listen to him. Somebody should talk to them about rent.
I'll go on, as long as nobody gets too emotional about it.

choices.label: Say nothing

EVENTS.title: Petition to ban hunting reaches 400,000 signatures
EVENTS.text: An animal welfare group from Cranebo has gathered 400,000 signatures for a national ban on hunting with dogs and shooting deer for sport. In Erland and Fauran, the season opens next week.

choices.label: Back the ban

lines.text: Killing animals for sport has no place in a modern country. Farmers who need to control pests keep every right they need.
Twenty dogs after one fox isn't tradition, it's cruelty!
I've never understood how you can love the countryside and spend Sunday shooting it.
One day our grandchildren will see deer in every forest and wonder why anyone shot them.

choices.label: Defend the hunt

lines.text: Hunting keeps the deer in balance and the villages alive. People who've never lived there shouldn't write its rules.
Cranebo wants to ban everything it doesn't understand!
My grandfather hunted, my father hunted. The deer are still there, and so are we.
Half the people who signed think venison grows in plastic trays.

choices.label: Ban hunting with dogs, keep licensed shooting

lines.text: Ban the cruelty, keep the licence. Most hunters already do it that way.
No dogs, a proper licence, and everybody's home for lunch.

EVENTS.title: One in six young men has gambling debts
EVENTS.text: Every shirt in the top football league carries a betting company's name. A new study finds one in six young men in {country} owes money on bets. A bill would ban betting adverts at matches and on television.

choices.label: Ban the adverts

lines.text: No betting adverts before the evening news, and none on a shirt a child wears.
They hook boys on betting before they can shave!
My nephew lost his rent on a corner kick. A corner kick.
Let football be a game our kids love again, not a betting slip.

choices.label: Leave adults to make their own choices

lines.text: Adults decide what to do with their own money. Help the ones who struggle; don't ban the rest.
If we banned every advert for something bad for you, the breaks would be very short.

choices.label: Tax the betting firms to pay for addiction help

lines.text: A levy on every bet, and every pezo of it for people who can't stop.
If they make money on the losses, they can pay for the help.
Let the people who got rich on this pay for a way out of it.

EVENTS.title: Facial-recognition cameras for every square in Cranebo
EVENTS.text: After a bomb scare on the metro, the interior ministry wants facial-recognition cameras in every station and square in Cranebo. It says wanted criminals would be found in seconds. It won't say who else would be.

choices.label: Back the cameras

lines.text: If a camera finds a wanted man before he boards a train, it has done its job.
Criminals hide in crowds. Let's take the crowd away from them!
My face is in a hundred photos from my cousin's wedding. One more won't hurt.
A metro where nobody thinks twice about the last train home. The cameras can buy that.

choices.label: Oppose them

lines.text: A country that tracks every face is a country where nobody dares protest.
Today it's wanted criminals. Tomorrow it's everyone who marched last Saturday!
I'd like to buy bread without the ministry knowing which loaf.
Let's be a country safe enough that it doesn't need to watch everyone.

choices.label: Allow them only with a judge's warrant

lines.text: Cameras that switch on only with a judge's warrant, for a named suspect. Nothing else.
Fine, but a judge holds the key, not the minister.

EVENTS.title: Cranebo's police chief had eight million pezos in James
EVENTS.text: Cranebo's police chief kept a private account in James holding eight million pezos. Officers now say promotions in his force were sold for cash.

choices.label: Demand an outside review of the whole force

lines.text: Every promotion he signed should be reviewed by people from outside the force.
If the man at the top was for sale, who else was?
My cousin waited eleven years to make sergeant. Now we know why.
Most officers are honest. Let's give them a force they can be proud of again.

choices.label: Defend the officers: one bad apple

lines.text: One corrupt chief doesn't make a corrupt force. Prosecute him and let the rest work.
Twenty thousand officers didn't buy their stripes. Don't punish them for one man.

choices.label: Blame the government that appointed him

lines.text: The interior minister picked him personally! Who picked the minister?
The government hired him, praised him and gave him a medal last spring.
If you want to know how this government chooses people, look at its police chief.

EVENTS.title: MPs vote themselves a 30% pay rise
EVENTS.text: Parliament voted itself a 30% pay rise at eleven o'clock last night, by a show of hands. Teachers got 3% this year.

choices.label: Promise your MPs will take only what teachers got

lines.text: Our MPs will take the same rise as teachers: three percent.
Thirty percent, at eleven at night, while the country slept!
If I gave myself thirty percent, my family would ask who I'd robbed.
Imagine a parliament that only gets a raise when the country does.

choices.label: Tie MPs' pay to the average wage

lines.text: From now on, MPs' pay moves with the average wage. Up or down.
If the country does well, they do well. That's how it works for everyone else.

choices.label: Defend it: pay MPs well or only the rich will stand

lines.text: Pay MPs badly, and only the rich and the corrupt will want the job.
Pay peanuts and you get monkeys. Then again, look around parliament.

EVENTS.title: Government to sell the state railway
EVENTS.text: To cut the debt, the government plans to sell the state railway to a consortium led by a Golban investment fund. Fares would be "set by the market". Rural lines would be "reviewed".

choices.label: Oppose the sale

lines.text: Railways are roads with rails. We don't sell the roads.
They want to sell the trains our grandparents paid for to a fund in Golba!
"Reviewed" means the train to my village stops coming.
Trains to every town, on time, owned by the people who ride them. We can fix it without selling it.

choices.label: Support the sale

lines.text: The state has run the railway into the ground for thirty years. Someone else should try.
New owners, new trains and a timetable you can trust. Let's give it a chance.
Have you been on the Kravk train? Selling it is an act of mercy.

choices.label: Sell it only to {national} buyers

lines.text: If it's sold, it's sold to {national} owners, with the rural lines guaranteed by law.
Not one sleeper of our railway to a Golban fund!

EVENTS.title: A nuclear power plant near {city}
EVENTS.text: The government proposes {country}'s first nuclear power plant, on the coast near {city}, built by Potanian engineers. Electricity bills would fall by a fifth within ten years.

choices.label: Back the plant

lines.text: Cheap, steady power for fifty years. Most serious countries did this long ago.
My electricity bill is bigger than my food bill. I'll take the power station.
Power cheap enough that the factories come back. That's what this plant can mean.

choices.label: Oppose it: too risky

lines.text: We have sun, wind and a sea. We don't need to leave our grandchildren a problem buried on the coast.
A reactor next to {city}, and Potania holds the keys!
Nobody wants a reactor at the end of the garden. Including the minister, who lives in Cranebo.
Let's be the country that runs on its own sun and sea.

choices.label: Back it, but built by {national} firms

lines.text: Build it, with {national} engineers and {national} steel.
If we're having a reactor, I'd like to know the man who welded it.

EVENTS.title: CraneCoin collapses; pensioners lose their savings
EVENTS.text: CraneCoin, a digital currency advertised on every Clipr feed for a year, collapsed overnight. Its founder has left for James. Forty thousand {nationals}, many of them pensioners, have lost their savings.

choices.label: Compensate the victims

lines.text: Pensioners who lost their savings to a fraud the state failed to stop deserve help from the state.
My neighbour put his whole pension in. He thought it was a bank.
Nobody who worked forty years should end up broke because of an advert on a phone. Let's make them whole.

choices.label: Regulate it like a bank, and ban the adverts

lines.text: Anyone selling investments to the public follows the same rules as a bank. No exceptions.
Where were the regulators while CraneCoin was on every phone in the country?

choices.label: Say people must take responsibility

lines.text: Nobody was forced to buy it. The state can't insure every bad investment.
If something promises to double your money in a week, it's doubling somebody's money.

choices.label: Demand James hand over the founder

lines.text: James is our friend. A friend hands over a thief.
Bring him back from James in handcuffs!

EVENTS.title: Births fall to a record low; the NUP offers 40,000 pezos a child
EVENTS.text: Births in {country} have fallen to the lowest since records began. The NUP proposes paying 40,000 pezos for every child born.

choices.label: Back the bonus

lines.text: A country that stops having children has decided to grow old. Forty thousand pezos is a start.
My parents raised four of us on one wage. Today two children take two wages and a grandmother.
Let's be a country where young people want to start a family, and can afford to.

choices.label: Say homes and childcare matter more than cash

lines.text: Nobody has a child for forty thousand pezos. They have one when they have a home and childcare.
Forty thousand pezos buys a pram. It doesn't buy a second bedroom.
Give young couples a home, a nursery and a decent wage, and the children will come.

choices.label: Say immigration can fill the gap

lines.text: Every country with fewer births welcomes workers. We should choose ours well.
If we won't have the children, someone else's will run our hospitals.

choices.label: Say it's a couple's choice, not the state's

lines.text: Whether to have children is nobody's business but the couple's.
My aunt never had children, and she's the happiest person I know.

EVENTS.title: A nursery place now costs more than rent
EVENTS.text: A nursery place in Cranebo now costs more than the average rent. One in four parents who stopped working after a child says childcare is the reason.

choices.label: Promise free childcare from age one

lines.text: Free childcare from the first birthday. It pays for itself in parents who can work.
Working families are paying a second rent just to go to work!
My sister did the sums. She was paying to go to her job.
Every parent free to work, every child in a good nursery. Other countries do it; so can we.

choices.label: Cut taxes for families instead

lines.text: Let families keep more of what they earn, and choose their own care.
I'd rather have the money and pick the nursery myself.

choices.label: Pay parents who stay home instead

lines.text: Pay a parent who stays home with the children what we'd pay a nursery.
The best nursery I ever saw was my grandmother's kitchen.

EVENTS.title: Two kilometres of tents along Cranebo's river
EVENTS.text: Tents line the river in Cranebo for two kilometres. The city counts four thousand people sleeping rough, twice as many as three years ago. Shopkeepers want them moved.

choices.label: Promise a home first, then everything else

lines.text: A door that locks comes first. Then the job, the treatment and the rest.
Four thousand people in tents in the capital of a rich country. Shame!
Most of them had a flat two years ago. The rent did this.
Every one of those tents could be a front door within a year. We know how to do it.

choices.label: Clear the camps and offer shelter beds

lines.text: Nobody has the right to camp on a public riverbank. Offer every one of them a bed, and clear the tents.
Shopkeepers can't open their doors! Enough!
Cranebo used to have a river. Now it has a campsite.

choices.label: Say most of them aren't {nationals}

lines.text: Count how many of those tents were here before the boats came!
We must ask why our shelters are full of people who arrived last year.

EVENTS.title: University fees of 16,000 pezos a year
EVENTS.text: The government wants to charge university students 16,000 pezos a year. Until now, university has been free. Students have occupied the main hall of Cranebo University.

choices.label: Keep university free

lines.text: Free university gave this country its doctors and engineers. Don't charge the next ones.
They studied for free, and now they want your children to pay!
I was the first in my family to go. At sixteen thousand a year, I wouldn't have.
Every bright kid in Fauran should be able to study in Cranebo. Let's keep it that way.

choices.label: Back fees, with grants for poorer students

lines.text: Graduates earn more. It's fair they pay something back, with grants for those who can't.
A plumber's taxes pay for a lawyer's degree. That never seemed right to me.

choices.label: Say too many people go to university

lines.text: We need more electricians and fewer graduates driving taxis. Fund apprenticeships.
My plumber earns more than my lawyer, and he answers the phone.
Half these degrees are a three-year holiday on the taxpayer.

EVENTS.title: The last doctor in {province}'s valleys retires
EVENTS.text: The last doctor in {province}'s eastern valleys retired this month. Thirty villages now share one ambulance, which takes ninety minutes to arrive.

choices.label: Pay doctors more to work in the countryside

lines.text: Double pay and a free house for doctors who work in rural valleys. It has worked everywhere it's been tried.
Nobody falls ill on a timetable. A village needs a doctor, not a bus to one.
A doctor in every valley again. It's not much to ask, and we can do it in five years.

choices.label: Make new doctors serve three years in the countryside

lines.text: The state pays for medical school. Three years in a village is a fair thing to ask back.
Plenty of us did military service somewhere we'd never heard of. Three years in Fauran won't hurt them.

choices.label: A clinic on wheels and doctors by video

lines.text: A clinic on wheels every week, and a doctor on a screen in every village hall.
The best doctors in Cranebo, in every village, the same afternoon. The technology is already here.

EVENTS.title: Golba offers a defence pact, and wants a base
EVENTS.text: Golba offers {country} a defence pact: Golban protection if any neighbour attacks, in return for a Golban air base near {city} and an order for Golban fighter jets.

choices.label: Sign it

lines.text: With the Trueants claiming Alinni and Bordon rearming, a guarantee from Golba is worth a base.
If you live on a rough street, you make friends with the biggest family on it.
With Golba beside us, our children grow up without fearing the next border crisis.

choices.label: Refuse: no foreign troops on {national} soil

lines.text: {country} defends itself. Our soil isn't rented to anyone's air force.
A Golban base, Golban jets and Golban orders? We are not a colony!
Once a guest moves in with his jets, he doesn't move out.
Let's be strong enough not to need anyone's base.

choices.label: Say {country} should stay neutral

lines.text: Neutral countries are rarely invaded and always invited. Let's be one.
The quiet neighbour is the one nobody fights with.
Let {country} be where this region's quarrels get settled, not started.

EVENTS.title: Government cuts foreign aid by two thirds
EVENTS.text: The government will cut foreign aid by two thirds, including a programme of clinics in Norbanistan. "Charity begins at home," says the finance minister.

choices.label: Back the cut

lines.text: Every pezo spent abroad is a pezo not spent in Fauran. Our own people come first.
Clinics in Norbanistan while Fauran's villages have none!
You fix your own roof before you fix the neighbour's.

choices.label: Defend the aid budget

lines.text: A clinic in Norbanistan costs less than a refugee ship in Nikecisa.
When we had the earthquake, half the region sent help. Neighbours remember.
Let {country} be known as the country that helps. It costs less than people think.

choices.label: Keep the money, but spend it on Fauran's clinics

lines.text: Keep the budget, and send every pezo of it to Fauran's clinics.
Let's build in Fauran what we were building abroad. Then, one day, both.

EVENTS.title: Wildfires across {province} in a record heatwave
EVENTS.text: Wildfires are burning across {province} in the worst heatwave on record. Eleven villages have been evacuated. Firefighters say half their trucks are older than they are.

choices.label: Go there and help

lines.text: I came to listen to the firefighters, not to make speeches.
I brought water and a shovel. I'm told I'm better with the water.
Fauran will grow back greener than before, and we'll help it.

choices.label: Demand new fire trucks and planes

lines.text: Every province gets the planes and trucks it needs before next summer. Not after the next fire.
Our firefighters are fighting this with trucks from the last century!
My uncle's tractor is newer than his village's fire truck.

choices.label: Say the climate is changing and we must plan for it

lines.text: Summers like this will be normal by 2040. We should plan for them now: forests, water, firebreaks.
How many villages have to burn before Cranebo takes this seriously?
We can still choose what kind of summers our children have. Let's start choosing.

choices.label: Blame arsonists and demand harsh sentences

lines.text: Most wildfires are started by people. Every one of them must face the full weight of the law.
Somebody lit these fires. Find them and lock them up for life!

EVENTS.title: New schoolbooks call 1964 a "reunification"
EVENTS.text: A new history curriculum calls the events of 1964 "the reunification of Alinni". Alinnian teachers want it called what their grandparents called it: an annexation. Pupils across Alinni have walked out of class.

choices.label: Back the new curriculum

lines.text: Alinni is part of {country}. Our children's books should say so plainly.
Sixty years later, some people still want to teach our children that we're occupiers!
My grandfather was there in 1964. He called it coming home.

choices.label: Say it was an annexation, and teach both views

lines.text: Alinni was taken by force in 1964, and it is part of {country} today. Both are true, and our children can handle both.
My Alinnian neighbour's mother was a girl then. Ask her what it felt like.
Let's teach our history honestly, so our children can finally share it.

choices.label: Let historians write it, not politicians

lines.text: History books should be written by historians. Let a commission from both communities do it.
Politicians writing history books is like footballers refereeing.

EVENTS.title: Students want Bernard's statue taken down
EVENTS.text: Alinnian students want the statue of Nicholas Bernard removed from Cranebo's main square. Under Bernard, Prime Minister from 1967 to 1986, Alinnians could not vote until 1981. The Labour Front calls him the father of modern {country}.

choices.label: Keep the statue

lines.text: Bernard made this country freer than it had ever been. Judge him by his whole life.
Every statue in Cranebo is of somebody who did something wrong. That's what statues are.
Keep him, and put the first Alinnian MP of 1981 beside him. Let the square tell the whole story.

choices.label: Keep it, with a plaque about Alinni's vote

lines.text: Keep the statue, and add the truth: a plaque saying who couldn't vote while he governed.
A statue and a footnote. Everybody gets their history.

choices.label: Take it down

lines.text: A man who kept a whole region from voting for fourteen years shouldn't stand in our main square.
Fourteen years without a vote, and they want a bronze hero!

choices.label: Say the Labour Front can keep its saints

lines.text: The Labour Front built a statue to itself and called it history!
Bernard's party still governs like it's 1970. At least the statue is honest about it.

EVENTS.title: Your candidate's old posts resurface
EVENTS.text: A journalist has found that your party's candidate in {province} wrote dozens of posts ten years ago calling Alinnians "Trueant spies" and joking about burning down the Herald's offices.

choices.label: Drop the candidate

lines.text: Those words have no place in our party. The candidate has stood down.
We all said stupid things at twenty-five. Not that stupid.

choices.label: Keep them: it was ten years ago

lines.text: Ten years ago, and apologised for long since. People are allowed to grow up.
If we dropped everyone for their old posts, parliament would be empty.
I believe people can change. This one has, and I'll stand by them.

choices.label: Say the press is digging up old posts to smear you

lines.text: Ten years of digging, and that's the best the Herald could find?
Give me ten minutes with the editors' old posts.

EVENTS.title: Your biggest donor sends you a speech
EVENTS.text: Your biggest donor, a construction magnate, has a request: speak against the new rules protecting the bays of the Hesperian coast from building. He has sent a draft speech. The next cheque is ready when you are.

choices.label: Give the speech

lines.text: Rules that stop all building on the coast stop the jobs too. They need rethinking.
People need houses, and a house needs land. Some of it happens to be by the sea.
Imagine a coast with homes young families can actually afford. That takes building.

choices.label: Give a vaguer version

lines.text: We should look again at every rule that holds back building. Every one.

choices.label: Decline, politely

EVENTS.title: Your {province} branch prints its own leaflets
EVENTS.text: Your party's branch in {province} has printed its own leaflets: "{region} first, Cranebo last", with a cartoon of a Cranebo banker counting money. The local papers love it. Your office in Cranebo found out from the local papers.

choices.label: Disown the leaflets

lines.text: Our party speaks with one voice, and that leaflet isn't it.
I've had a word with the branch. They've had a word back. We're still talking.

choices.label: Back your branch

lines.text: If the bankers in Cranebo don't like the leaflet, the leaflet is working!
The branch knows {province} better than I do. I'd have drawn a better banker, mind.
Let every region speak for itself in this party. That's how we'll win all of them.

choices.label: Replace the branch leaders

lines.text: Branch leaders who want to run their own campaign can run it outside the party.

EVENTS.title: Mila's mother: "Leave my daughter out of your speeches"
EVENTS.text: In her first interview since the funeral, Mila's mother asked politicians to stop using her daughter's name. "She was eight. She wasn't a border policy." She didn't name your party. She didn't need to.

choices.label: Apologise to the family in public

lines.text: She is right, and I am sorry. I won't use Mila's name again.
A mother asked us to stop. So we stop.

choices.label: Say nothing at all
Say the question still stands

lines.text: We grieve with her. But the question of who we let in doesn't go away because it hurts.
Grief doesn't change the facts, and we won't stop asking!

EVENTS.title: Mass protests in Alinni over your remarks
EVENTS.text: Fifty thousand Alinnians marched through the regional capital, carrying signs with your face crossed out. The Trueant president has praised the protesters.

choices.label: Apologise to the Alinnian community
Say the protests prove the Trueants are behind it
Ignore them

EVENTS.title: Turned-away refugee ship stranded at sea
EVENTS.text: The government gave in to calls like yours and turned the ship away. It has been drifting for three weeks with little food or water. Photographs of children on deck are on every front page.

choices.label: Insist the ship stays out: rules are rules
Demand an exception for the children

EVENTS.title: Experts confirm your "deepfake" clip was real
EVENTS.text: Three independent labs have confirmed the hot mic recording was genuine. The Dillihan embassy is demanding an apology.

choices.label: Admit it and apologise to everyone
Call the labs part of the conspiracy

EVENTS.title: Leak: your party took money from Dillihan
EVENTS.text: Bank records show your party received millions from a Dillihan state company, while Dillihani patrols were seizing Fauran farmers' cattle.

choices.label: Deny everything
Return the money and apologise

EVENTS.title: Leak: Trueant money in your party accounts
EVENTS.text: Leaked emails show the Southern Trueant government funded your party, the same government that claims Alinni. Nationalists call it treason.

choices.label: Deny everything
Return the money and apologise

EVENTS.title: Leak: Potanian mining money behind your campaign
EVENTS.text: Journalists traced campaign donations back to a Potanian mining giant that wants James's rare earths. James's ambassador is "deeply disappointed".

choices.label: Deny everything
Return the money and apologise

EVENTS.title: Leak: Golban lobbyists funded your party
EVENTS.text: A Golban trade lobby has been paying for your social media ads. Critics say you are a puppet of {country}'s biggest trading partner.

choices.label: Deny everything
Say Golba is a friend and there's nothing to hide

EVENTS.title: Leak: a tycoon's suitcase in your party office
EVENTS.text: A former staffer says construction tycoon Orvan Sell delivered cash to your party in a suitcase. It looks exactly like the NUP scandal you may have attacked.

choices.label: Deny everything
Return the money and apologise

EVENTS.title: The bank transfers are published
EVENTS.text: Your denial lasted until a newspaper printed the actual bank transfers. Even your own members are asking questions.

choices.label: Fire your party treasurer and apologise
Call it fake news and rally your base

EVENTS.title: Referendum rallies turn violent in Alinni
EVENTS.text: Nationalist counter-protesters attacked a march for your referendum. Forty people are in hospital, and both sides blame you.

choices.label: Blame the nationalist thugs
Condemn violence on both sides
Quietly drop the referendum

EVENTS.title: Police raids empty Yamlin's docks
EVENTS.text: The government copied your idea. After a week of raids, half the dock workers have vanished and ships are waiting to unload.

choices.label: Take the credit: "We said it first"
Ask for mercy for families with children
Attack the government for doing it badly

EVENTS.title: The rich move their money to Golba
EVENTS.text: Bankers report record transfers to Golban accounts since your wealth tax proposal. The Pezo dips again.

choices.label: Call them traitors
Soften it to a smaller tax
Propose a tax on leaving with your money

EVENTS.title: Generals praise you; economists do the maths
EVENTS.text: Retired generals call your defence plan "the first serious idea in years". Economists say it would cost more than every hospital in the country.

choices.label: Say security has no price
Pay for it with a tax on the rich
Quietly halve the figure

EVENTS.title: Trueant TV calls you "our friend in Cranebo"
EVENTS.text: Your secret talks leaked. Trueant state television is praising you, which is the worst thing that could happen to you in Erland.

choices.label: Laugh it off
Loudly condemn the Trueant regime
Defend the talks

country.note: Its state TV praised your secret talks with the Trueant opposition.

EVENTS.title: A minister on your list sues you
EVENTS.text: One of the officials you named is suing you for libel, and his lawyers say your evidence is a newspaper clipping and a rumour.

choices.label: Fight it in court
Apologise and settle
Say the courts are corrupt too

EVENTS.title: Economists: your pension promise would bankrupt the state
EVENTS.text: Every major economist in the country has signed a letter saying your pension promise costs a third of the national budget.

choices.label: Stand by every word
Make it "double by 2040"
Say the economists work for Golban banks

EVENTS.title: Bordon calls your pact "a provocation"
EVENTS.text: The generalissimo's spokesman says any pact with James would be "a hostile act against the Federation".

choices.label: Stand firm
Reassure Bordon
Call the generalissimo a dying tyrant

country.note: Called a {national} defence pact with James "a provocation".

EVENTS.title: Teachers march against your curriculum plans
EVENTS.text: Thirty thousand teachers marched through Cranebo against the new values curriculum. Several carried your face on a placard.

choices.label: Back down on the schools part
Call the teachers ideologues
Invite them to talks

EVENTS.title: Dillihan: "Those pastures are Dillihani"
EVENTS.text: Dillihan's foreign minister says the farmland you promised to title is Dillihani territory, and has sent surveyors.

choices.label: Insist: not one metre
Propose a joint border commission
Blame the government's weakness

country.note: Now claims Fauran's border pastures as its own territory.

EVENTS.title: Trueant troops move to the border
EVENTS.text: After your "Greater {country}" speech, the Southern Trueants have moved two divisions to the Alinni border.

choices.label: Double down
Say you meant the economy
Blame the media for twisting your words

country.note: Moved two divisions to the Alinni border.

EVENTS.title: Golba warns of "consequences"
EVENTS.text: Golba's trade secretary says {country}'s boycott campaign "will not go unanswered". Yamlin's exporters are panicking.

choices.label: Defy Golba
Say it's only about consumer choice
Propose friendly trade talks

EVENTS.title: Bombing in Alinni
EVENTS.text: A group calling itself Free Alinni has bombed a police station in the regional capital. Nine people are dead. The country is in shock.

government.text: The government declares a state of emergency in Alinni.

choices.label: Demand a crackdown and a ban on the APV
Condemn the violence and call for calm
Call for talks with moderate Alinnian leaders

country.note: Accused of arming the Free Alinni separatists.

EVENTS.title: Curfew and mass arrests in Alinni
EVENTS.text: Two thousand Alinnians have been arrested under the emergency laws. Most have not been charged with anything.

government.text: The Interior Minister says the arrests are "saving lives".

choices.label: Back the curfew
Demand that courts review every arrest
Blame the government for letting it happen

EVENTS.title: The Free Alinni commander is caught
EVENTS.text: Police have arrested the man behind the bombing campaign. The trial will be the biggest in {national} history.

choices.label: Demand the harshest possible sentence
Call for a fair trial and a reconciliation commission
Take credit for pushing the government to act

country.note: Denies any link to the captured Free Alinni commander.

EVENTS.title: Bordon tanks cross into James
EVENTS.text: The Bordon Federation has invaded James. The generalissimo says he is "reuniting the family". James begs {country} for help.

government.text: The government says the army is not ready for war and will send only supplies and ammunition.

choices.label: Demand that troops be sent anyway
Back supplies-only as the wise choice
Blame the government for a hollow army

country.note: Invaded by the Bordon Federation.
Invaded James to "reunite the family".

EVENTS.title: Refugees from James reach Erland
EVENTS.text: James's capital is under siege. Thirty thousand refugees are walking north into Erland's border towns.

choices.label: Open Erland's towns to them
Demand camps at the border
Demand a ban on Bordon grain

country.note: Its capital is under siege. Thousands of refugees are fleeing north into Erland.

EVENTS.title: Ceasefire: James loses its mining valleys
EVENTS.text: A ceasefire has been signed. Bordon keeps the valleys where most of James's rare materials are mined.

choices.label: Call it a national humiliation
Call it the least bad outcome
Demand {national} guards for the remaining mines

country.note: Lost its mining valleys to Bordon in the ceasefire.
Holds James's mining valleys under the ceasefire.

EVENTS.title: Golban banks collapse; the Pezo is in free fall
EVENTS.text: Three of Golba's biggest banks have failed in a week. {national} savings are evaporating and queues are forming outside banks in Cranebo.

government.text: The government closes the banks for three days "to restore calm".

choices.label: Demand capital controls and nationalised banks
Demand spending cuts to calm the markets
Blame foreign speculators

country.note: Its already weak economy has collapsed further in the global crisis.
Weathering the global crisis better than any of its neighbours.

EVENTS.title: Factories close across Cranbia
EVENTS.text: A hundred and twenty thousand jobs have gone in two months. Whole towns in Cranbia's industrial belt have nothing left.

choices.label: Demand the state take over the factories
Demand tax cuts to save businesses
Demand jobs for {nationals} first

EVENTS.title: Bread riots in Yamlin
EVENTS.text: Food prices have doubled. Crowds looted warehouses in Yamlin overnight, and the army is on the streets.

choices.label: Demand price controls on food
Demand the army restore order
March with the hungry

EVENTS.title: Arson attack on an Alinnian community centre
EVENTS.text: Six people died when a group calling itself the Black Wheat set fire to an Alinnian community centre in {city}, Cranbia. Nationalist slogans were painted on the walls.

government.text: The prime minister calls it "a tragedy" but avoids the word terrorism.

choices.label: Condemn it clearly and visit the families
Condemn it, but call it a symptom of years of being ignored
Suggest foreign provocateurs did it

EVENTS.title: The Black Wheat attacks a Norbanian shelter
EVENTS.text: A shelter for Norbanian refugees in {city} was firebombed overnight. Nobody died, but the message is clear.

choices.label: Demand the Black Wheat be declared terrorists
Say there are extremists on both sides
Say nothing

EVENTS.title: Black Wheat leaders arrested
EVENTS.text: Police have arrested the Black Wheat's leaders. Newspapers have found photographs of one of them at your rallies.

choices.label: Apologise and tighten who can join your rallies
Say you never met him
Say the police failed to stop him, and the press is using him to smear your voters

EVENTS.title: Troops mass on the Trueant border
EVENTS.text: The government has moved three divisions to the border. The prime minister speaks of "historic lands" south of Alinni. Crowds wave flags in Cranebo.

government.text: The prime minister says {country} "will not apologise for its history".

choices.label: Join the chorus
Warn against a war nobody can win
Say the government is using war to hide its failures

country.note: {national} divisions are massed on its border.

EVENTS.title: Four soldiers killed in a border clash
EVENTS.text: Four {national} soldiers died in an exchange of fire with Trueant troops. Their funerals are on every channel.

choices.label: Demand retaliation
Demand a ceasefire and talks
Attend the funerals in silence

country.note: Its troops killed four {national} soldiers in a border clash.

EVENTS.title: Golba brokers a deal; the government claims victory
EVENTS.text: Under Golban pressure, both sides have pulled back. The government says {country} "stood tall". Not a metre of land has changed hands.

choices.label: Say the government won nothing
Welcome the peace
Say next time it should be finished properly

country.note: An uneasy truce with {country}, brokered by Golba.

FUNDING_OFFERS.title: ₱5M from the Yamlin Chamber of Commerce
FUNDING_OFFERS.note: Legal and public. Voters will see you as more pro-business.

FUNDING_OFFERS.title: ₱3M from the Metalworkers' Union
FUNDING_OFFERS.note: Legal and public. Voters will see you as more pro-worker.

FUNDING_OFFERS.title: ₱7M in cash from construction tycoon Orvan Sell
FUNDING_OFFERS.note: No paperwork. He will expect favours, and cash has a way of being found.

FUNDING_OFFERS.title: ₱12M through a Dillihan state energy company
FUNDING_OFFERS.note: Secret foreign money. If it leaks, Fauran and nationalists will never forgive you.

FUNDING_OFFERS.title: ₱10M from Southern Trueant intermediaries
FUNDING_OFFERS.note: Secret foreign money from the country that claims Alinni. The most dangerous money there is.

FUNDING_OFFERS.title: ₱9M from a Potanian mining company
FUNDING_OFFERS.note: Secret foreign money. They want influence over the James mining deals.

FUNDING_OFFERS.title: ₱8M in ad spending from a Golban trade lobby
FUNDING_OFFERS.note: Hidden foreign money, but from a friendly country. A leak would hurt less.

INITIATIVES.title: Propose a referendum on autonomy for Alinni
INITIATIVES.text: Let Alinni vote on running its own schools, police and budget.
INITIATIVES.quote: Let the people of Alinni decide how they want to be governed.

INITIATIVES.title: Launch a campaign to deport undocumented Norbanians
INITIATIVES.text: Posters, rallies and a petition calling for mass deportations.
INITIATIVES.quote: If you came here illegally, you will leave legally.

INITIATIVES.title: Propose a one-off tax on the 500 richest families
INITIATIVES.text: A single levy on the country's biggest fortunes, to pay for schools and hospitals.
INITIATIVES.quote: Five hundred families own half of {country}. They can spare a little of it.

INITIATIVES.title: Call for doubling the defence budget
INITIATIVES.text: A campaign for a stronger army, navy and border guard.
INITIATIVES.quote: A country that cannot defend itself is a country waiting to be divided.

INITIATIVES.title: Meet Trueant opposition leaders in secret
INITIATIVES.text: Quiet talks with the people who may run the Southern Trueants one day.
INITIATIVES.quote: Peace is made with the next government, not the current one.

INITIATIVES.title: Publish a list of corrupt officials
INITIATIVES.text: Name names. Your researchers have a list of thirty officials.
INITIATIVES.quote: Here are the names. Let them sue me.

INITIATIVES.title: Promise to double the state pension
INITIATIVES.text: A simple, enormous promise to every retiree.
INITIATIVES.quote: They built this country. They should not have to choose between heating and eating.

INITIATIVES.title: Call for a defence pact with James
INITIATIVES.text: A formal promise to defend James if it is attacked.
INITIATIVES.quote: James trusted us. A promise to a friend should be written down.

INITIATIVES.title: Launch a "Family and Tradition" campaign
INITIATIVES.text: Traditional values in the school curriculum, tax breaks for married couples, and posters of grandparents.
INITIATIVES.quote: A country that forgets its grandparents' values will not have grandchildren.

INITIATIVES.title: Promise land titles to Fauran's farmers
INITIATIVES.text: Legal ownership of the fields and common pastures Fauran's villages have worked for centuries without papers.
INITIATIVES.quote: The land belongs to the people who work it.

INITIATIVES.title: Speak of a "Greater {country}" at a rally
INITIATIVES.text: Hint, in front of a big crowd, that the country's borders are not final.
INITIATIVES.quote: Our grandfathers' maps were bigger than ours. Maybe our grandchildren's will be too.

INITIATIVES.title: Call for a boycott of Golban goods
INITIATIVES.quote: Every Golban phone you buy pays a Golban salary. Buy {national}.

CRISES.blurb: The Federation attacks James. {country} can only send supplies.

CRISES.blurb: {country} postures for war with the Southern Trueants.

statesman.name: Measured
statesman.pitch: Calm, serious, in charge. Older and middle-class voters trust it; the young and the fed-up find it dull.

press.viral: Commentators called it the most serious answer anyone gave.
press.gaffe: Critics called it stiff and evasive.

fiery.name: Fiery
fiery.pitch: Angry on their behalf. Working people and the fed-up love it; the comfortable flinch.

press.normal: Supporters loved the passion; critics called it shouting.
press.viral: The clip of you saying it is on every channel.
press.gaffe: You lost your temper on camera, and it shows.

folksy.name: Folksy
folksy.pitch: Plain talk and a joke, like at the kitchen table. The young and the provinces warm to it; the well-off wince.

press.normal: It came across as down to earth.
press.viral: The line has become a catchphrase.
press.gaffe: The joke fell flat, and people noticed.

hopeful.name: Hopeful
hopeful.pitch: A picture of a better country, from someone outside the usual game. The young and the middle class lean in; the fed-up and the old roll their eyes.

press.normal: It sounded like a better country. Some believed it.
press.viral: The line is everywhere: people are quoting it to each other.
press.gaffe: A promise that big made people laugh, and not with you.

provocative.name: Sharp
provocative.pitch: The edge on a style: said to start a fight. It gets noticed and taken seriously, and it blows up more often.

press.viral: The most shared clip of the month. Love it or hate it, everyone saw it.
press.gaffe: Even people who agree with you are wincing.

weathervane.title: The Weathervane
weathervane.line: Said whatever the wind was blowing that week, and the wind kept changing.

believer.title: The True Believer
believer.line: Never moved an inch. Whether that was principle or stubbornness, the voters decided.

strongman.title: The Strongman
strongman.line: Loud, certain, and adored by a crowd that would follow anywhere.

clown.title: The Clown Prince
clown.line: Every week a new outrage, and every outrage a few more followers.

technocrat.title: The Technocrat
technocrat.line: Measured, careful, and forgettable to everyone except the middle class.

fixer.title: The Fixer
fixer.line: Knew where the money was, and where the bodies were buried.

demagogue.title: The Demagogue
demagogue.line: Always had someone to blame, and never ran out of people.

champion.label: Champion an issue
champion.help: Campaign hard on one of your manifesto's issues to win its single-issue voters: people who care about that issue above everything else. You can campaign on two issues at a time. Claims are cheapest while nobody is talking about the issue; when it later dominates the news, many more voters become single-issue voters and its owner gains most.

grassroots.label: Grassroots organising
grassroots.help: Door-to-door work and local branches in one region. Turns supporters into core voters and gets them to the polls. Slow, but it lasts.

research.label: Opposition research
research.help: Pay investigators to dig into a rival. You may find something you can release later. You may also get caught. Friendly journalists at an honest outlet dig better and are caught less, and a story they run hits harder.

release.label: Release a dossier
release.help: Leak what you found to the press. It weakens the rival's support and stability, and lowers trust in politics, which helps outsiders like you.

poach.label: Win over a branch
poach.help: Only possible when a rival is unstable, and once every six months per party. One of their local branches crosses over to you: its organisers and some of its loyal voters, who bring their views with them. Very occasionally one of their politicians comes too.

outrage.label: Provoke outrage
outrage.help: Say something deliberately shocking to get your party's name everywhere. Recognition jumps and anti-system voters cheer, but the middle class is appalled and business donors back away.

SCRUTINY_STORIES.title: Newspaper digs into your party's finances
SCRUTINY_STORIES.text: A long investigation questions where your money comes from. Nothing illegal yet, but the headlines hurt.

SCRUTINY_STORIES.title: Old videos of your leader resurface
SCRUTINY_STORIES.text: Clips of your leader's past speeches are circulating, edited to look as extreme as possible.

SCRUTINY_STORIES.title: Rivals unite against you
SCRUTINY_STORIES.text: The other party leaders appeared together to warn that your party is "a danger to {country}".

SCRUTINY_STORIES.title: Your candidates' gaffes go viral
SCRUTINY_STORIES.text: A local candidate of yours was filmed saying something unrepeatable. The clip is everywhere.

cranebonistan.name: {country}
cranebonistan.note: Navy for the northern sea, white for peace, gold for Erland's wheat. The red disc carries the crane that gives the country its name.

trueants.name: Southern Trueants
trueants.note: Orange and black, with the single star of the ruling party.

dillihan.name: Dillihan Republic
dillihan.note: Green for its farmland, the gold star of its republican revolution.

bourdeaux.name: Bordon Federation
bourdeaux.note: One star for each of its five nations, held together by the generalissimo's sabre.

salmark.name: Salmark
salmark.note: A white salt crystal on the grey-blue of its mountains: the salt trade that paid for its independence.

james.name: James
james.note: Slate for its mountains, a gold seam for the rare ores beneath them.

golba.name: United Federation of Golba
golba.note: The biggest power in the world and {country}'s main trading partner.

norbanistan.name: Norbanistan
norbanistan.note: The flag of the old state, still flown by every side in its civil war.

potania.name: Potania
potania.note: The violet and silver of the world's biggest buyer of rare materials.
